results.why: Flown straight at a no-fly zone. The Shield must never let it in.

The same flight unshielded. This scenario must FAIL its safety gate to be doing its job: if an unguarded run into a no-fly zone scores clean, the harness is measuring nothing and every other pass here is worthless.
Starts below the floor. Recovery must climb, not freeze.
Commanded to climb through the ceiling for the whole flight.
A pilot asking for 20 m/s against a 4 m/s cap.

A NaN command, which is one division away from any detector reporting a zero-width box. NaN loses every comparison, so an unsanitised action is declared legal and passed straight through - the guardrail failing OPEN.
A clean run down the middle. Nothing should be touched.
Aimed straight out of the side of the corridor.
The scheduled fence is in force on a Monday morning and must bind.

The same flight at 23:00. The fence is not in force, so the aircraft may fly through where it stood - and nothing may repair against it. A rule that still bends the action out of hours is enforcing a rule the policy says is off.
Flown at a declared pedestrian who is NOT on the route. The 10 m ring must hold and the mission must still finish.
THE ANSWER TO THE 2026-09-02 REVIEW, made measurable.

THE OPEN DEFECT, pinned here so it stops living only in a document. The subject sits exactly on the route, so every direction that makes progress also closes the range. The Shield never emits an illegal action - the P0 gate holds - but the mission wedges: the aircraft cannot get past the subject and never reaches its goal. Recorded on 2026-08-31 as the gap between "the action was repaired" and "the trajectory was sensible". When this scenario starts PASSING, the defect is fixed and the marker should come off.
